nb_greenlaw.blurb: Greenlaw is a small basalt cliff in the hills outside Saint Andrews, with single-pitch lines roughly 50 to 60 feet tall. The rock is vertical and fractured, and the climbing is almost all bolted sport, with a handful of trad lines. Grades run from easy cracks into the 5.12s, with a strong cluster of 5.11 and 5.12 sport routes. It sees little traffic, and shaded sections tend to grow moss and lichen, so some lines may want a brush and a dry spell before they climb well. Bring quickdraws and a rope for 60-foot pitches, plus a light rack if you want the easier trad. There is no water or other facilities at the cliff.
nb_greenlaw.parking_note: Pull off on the shoulder of Route 127 near the house numbered 3709 and leave room for residents and their driveways.
nb_greenlaw.approach: From the road a gated service road runs into the woods to a power line corridor. A marked trail leaving at pole 55 climbs to the right-hand end of the cliff, or you can keep following the corridor to an ATV track that reaches the wall further along. The final stretch is brushy and uneven.

nh_swamp_boulders_2.blurb: The Swamp Boulders are the largest cluster of problems in the Palmer Bartell Forest, a wooded preserve in Brookline with a network of trails and scattered, fairly spread-out bouldering. Nearly all of the climbing here is on boulders, and the grades lean friendly: most problems fall between VB and V3, with a smaller group of harder lines up into the V5 to V7 range. Expect a real walk in and some off-trail wandering to find the blocks, so bring a map or a saved track and a pad. A single top rope problem also exists. Damp ground near the swamp can make the base of some boulders soft after rain.
nh_swamp_boulders_2.parking_note: The forest trailhead is on Route 13 in Brookline, and a small signed lot there holds only a few cars.

nh_zoo_the.blurb: The Zoo is a dense group of boulders inside the Boulder Natural zone at Pawtuckaway, set in forest beside a small stream. It is known as a friendly place: a big share of the problems sit between V0 and V5, which makes it a good spot to warm up, work through a ladder of moderates, or spend a full day, while a few lines reach much higher. The boulders are highly featured with slopers and crimps. The zone is shady and slow to dry, and black flies and mosquitoes can be heavy in spring and early summer, so fall tends to be the most comfortable time.

nh_04_tier_3_boulders.blurb: Tier 3 is a newer set of boulders in the Sundown bouldering zone along the Kancamagus Highway, above the Tier 1 blocks. The problems cover a wide range, from V0 up to V8, with plenty in the middle grades and a solid group of V5 and harder lines for strong climbers. Surroundings are forested and quiet, and the Swift River and Lower Falls swimming area are close by. Many boulders in the wider zone have seen little traffic, so expect some moss or dirt on holds and consider a brush.
nh_04_tier_3_boulders.parking_note: Park near the Albany Covered Bridge off the Kancamagus Highway, where Passaconaway Road meets it. A lot at the Boulder Loop Trail start sits a short distance south of the bridge.

nh_upper_cliff.blurb: Upper Cliff is one of Pawtuckaway's main roped crags: a granite wall of mostly single-pitch trad cracks, with a few face lines between them that are usually climbed on top rope. The cracks start at easy fives and run well into the 5.10s and 5.11s, with most of the climbing in the 5.6 to 5.11 band. The wall is shaded and takes a while to dry after rain. Summer camps and family outings make it busy on weekends, and sturdy anchors above many lines make top-roping common. Stay on the established trails to protect the clifftop.
nh_upper_cliff.parking_note: Most visitors leave the car at the Horse Farm lot, reached from Route 156 and Deerfield Road, then walk the dirt road toward Round Pond.

nh_barber_wall.blurb: The Barber Wall is the upper left section of Cathedral Ledge above North Conway, a granite wall prized for crack climbing. Routes run from about 60 feet to nearly 200 feet, growing taller toward its far side. All of the climbing is trad, and most of it sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, which makes it a serious but rewarding training ground for hard cracks. Winter brings ice to much of the cliff. Take care when the rock is wet, and plan for exposure on the walk along the ledge to the base.

nh_7_the_slabs.blurb: The Slabs are the signature terrain of Whitehorse Ledge near North Conway: big, gently tilted granite aprons that rise from the woods behind a resort. Climbing here is about friction and footwork rather than holds, on long multi-pitch routes that can climb several hundred feet and sometimes more than a thousand feet of rope. Most routes are trad and fall between 5.5 and 5.10, and protection can be sparse, so route-finding and a calm head matter. It is a good choice for experienced climbers who want long moderates on traditional gear.

nh_07_main_cliff_boulders.blurb: These boulders collect in the talus field beneath the Main Cliff of Sundown Ledge, along the Kancamagus Highway. They offer a broad spread of problems from V0 into the double digits, with a lot of climbing in the V2 to V6 range and a few hard lines at the top end. Landings are often uneven in talus, so bring pads and a spotter. The setting is wooded and scenic, with the Swift River and a swimming area nearby, and some blocks see little traffic and may need brushing.
nh_07_main_cliff_boulders.parking_note: Park near the Albany Covered Bridge off the Kancamagus Highway, where Passaconaway Road meets it. A lot at the Boulder Loop Trail start sits a short distance south of the bridge.

nh_the_hinterlands.blurb: The Hinterlands is a large cliff in the upper reaches of Rumney, where the crags sit on the hillside of Rattlesnake Mountain. The schist here is steep and sharp, and the routes follow dikes, flakes, cracks and roofs. Most of the climbing is bolted sport, with a smaller number of trad lines and a few ice routes in winter. Grades run from about 5.6 to the low 5.12s, with a good concentration of 5.10s, so there are warm-ups as well as testpieces. The walk up from the parking areas is steep and rough, which keeps it quieter than the lower cliffs. Fall is the busiest season at Rumney.

nh_storm_boulders_the.blurb: The Storm Boulders are a group in the Boulder Natural zone at Pawtuckaway, in forest beside a stream, reached from the Round Pond side. Unlike the more moderate blocks nearby, the problems here lean hard: grades run from V2 to V11, with the bulk of them at V6 and above, so it suits strong boulderers working highballs and difficult lines. The rock is highly featured with slopers and crimps. The zone is shady and slow to dry, and insects are heavy in spring and early summer, which makes fall the best season.
